sentences.zh: 高敏，登州人。

translations.literal: Gao Min was a native of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Min came from Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 為涇原指使，數與西夏戰，遭重傷。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner of Jingyuan, fought the Western Xia many times, and suffered severe wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner of Jingyuan, fought the Western Xia repeatedly, and was gravely wounded more than once.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹、韓琦皆薦之，為閣門祗候，曆利州路、邠寧環慶都監，主蕃部事。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi both recommended him. He was made Gatehouse Attendant and successively served as superintendent of Lizhou Circuit and of Binning-Huanqing, overseeing tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi both recommended him. He was appointed Gatehouse Attendant and then served in turn as superintendent of Lizhou Circuit and of Binning-Huanqing, where he oversaw tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 羌圍大順城，偏將趙懷德力戰，其下以銀買級，主帥李復圭以所部不整欲治之。

translations.literal: When the Qiang besieged Dashuncheng, deputy general Zhao Huaide fought fiercely; his subordinates tried to buy exemption from punishment with silver. Commander Li Fugui wished to discipline them because his troops were disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang besieged Dashuncheng, deputy general Zhao Huaide fought hard; his men tried to buy their way out of punishment with silver. Commander Li Fugui wanted to punish them for the disorder in his ranks.

sentences.zh: 敏言懷德善用人，戰必勝，當略其小過，且蕃官難強以漢法，復圭乃止。

translations.literal: Min said Huaide was skilled at employing men and always won in battle; minor faults should be overlooked, and tribal officers could not be forced to submit to Han law. Fugui then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Min argued that Huaide knew how to use men and always won in battle, that his minor faults should be overlooked, and that tribal officers could not be forced to obey Han law. Fugui then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 羌人聲言將出鄜延，敏屢白復圭曰：「兵家之事，聲東擊西，環慶嘗破白豹、金湯，結釁已深，不可不備。

translations.literal: The Qiang announced they would strike through Fuyan. Min repeatedly reported to Fugui: "In military affairs one feints east while striking west. Huanqing has already taken Baibao and Jintang, and the feud runs deep—they must not go unguarded."
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang declared they would move through Fuyan. Min repeatedly warned Fugui: "In war one feints east and strikes west. Huanqing has already taken Baibao and Jintang, and the grudge runs deep—we cannot leave ourselves undefended."

sentences.zh: 」已而果以兵三十萬來寇。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they indeed came raiding with an army of three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they did indeed invade with an army of three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 總管楊遂駐兵大義，以敏為先鋒將。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Yang Sui held his army at Dayi and made Min vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commander Yang Sui encamped at Dayi and made Min his vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 夏人攻奪大順水砦，敏出通路，自寅及午，且戰且前，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: When the Xia seized the Dashun River fort, Min fought his way out through the passage from the hour yin to wu, advancing while battling, and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia captured the Dashun River fort, Min fought his way out through the pass from dawn to midday, advancing as he fought and taking many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 次榆林，援兵不至，中流矢死，年五十七。

translations.literal: At Yulin the relief force failed to arrive; he was struck by an arrow midstream and died at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: At Yulin the relief troops never came; he was struck by an arrow in midstream and died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 官止東頭供奉官。

translations.literal: His highest office was Eastern Head Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His highest rank was Eastern Head Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔贈嘉州刺史，錄其三子為侍禁、殿直。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him prefect of Jiazhou and enrolled his three sons as palace guards and as palace attendants of direct rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed him prefect of Jiazhou and enrolled his three sons as palace guards and as palace attendants of direct rank.

sentences.zh: 張吉者，慶州卒也，為淮安鎮守烽。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji was a soldier of Qingzhou, posted to Huai'an as a beacon watchman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was a soldier of Qingzhou, stationed at Huai'an to keep the beacon watch.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇東穀，掠得之，脅以兵，使呼城中曰：「淮安諸砦已破，宜速降。

translations.literal: When the Xia raided Donggu and captured him, they forced him at swordpoint to shout to the city: "All the Huai'an forts have fallen—you should surrender at once."
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided Donggu and captured him, they threatened him with arms and made him call to the city: "All the Huai'an forts have fallen—surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 」吉反其辭曰：「努力！

translations.literal: But Ji turned their words around and cried: "Stand firm!
translations.idiomatic: Ji turned their words against them and shouted: "Hold fast!

sentences.zh: 諸砦無虞，賊糧盡且去矣，毋庸降。

translations.literal: All the forts are safe! The bandits' grain is spent and they are about to withdraw—there is no need to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: The forts are all safe! The enemy's grain is spent and they are about to withdraw—do not surrender."

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，害之。

translations.literal: The enemy were enraged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were enraged and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈內殿崇班，又錄其子。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Inner Hall Distinguished Officer, and his son was also given office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Inner Hall Distinguished Officer and also granted office to his son.

sentences.zh: 景思忠，字進之，普州安嶽人。

translations.literal: Jing Sizhong, courtesy name Jinzhi, was a native of Anyue in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sizhong, styled Jinzhi, came from Anyue in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父西上閣門使泰蔭，累官西京左藏庫使，為遂州駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege as Western Upper Gate Commissioner Tai, he rose to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury and served as superintendent of the garrison at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege as Western Upper Gate Commissioner Tai, he rose to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury and served as superintendent of the garrison at Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 夷人寇淯井，鈐轄張承祐出兵救之，思忠部卒五百為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the barbarians raided Yu Jing, Controller Zhang Chengyou led troops to the rescue. Sizhong commandeered five hundred men as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians raided Yu Jing, Controller Zhang Chengyou marched out to the rescue. Sizhong led five hundred men as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 夷乘險薄官軍，官軍戰不利，死者十之六。

translations.literal: The barbarians used difficult terrain to press close on the government army; the fight went badly, and six out of ten were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians used the difficult ground to press in on the government army; the battle went badly, and six out of ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 左右勸思忠引避，不聽，奮劍疾戰而死。

translations.literal: Those around him urged Sizhong to withdraw; he would not listen, but drew his sword and fought fiercely until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him urged Sizhong to pull back, but he refused, drew his sword, and fought on until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 走馬使張宗望為言，詔察訪熊本考實，得其事，神宗憫之，官思忠及同死者之子七人，餘皆賜其家錢帛。

translations.literal: Palace Courier Zhang Zongwang spoke on his behalf. An edict ordered an investigation; Xiong Ben verified the facts. Emperor Shenzong took pity on him, granted offices to Sizhong and to the sons of seven who had died with him, and gave money and cloth to the rest of the families.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Courier Zhang Zongwang reported the matter. An edict ordered an investigation; Xiong Ben verified what had happened. Emperor Shenzong was moved with pity, granted offices to Sizhong and to the sons of seven men who had died with him, and gave money and cloth to the other families.

sentences.zh: 弟思立，以蔭主渭州治平砦。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sili, through yin privilege, commanded Zhiping Fort in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sili, through yin privilege, commanded Zhiping Fort in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 囉兀用兵，韓絳使攝保安軍。

translations.literal: During the Luowu campaign, Han Jiang had him act as superintendent of Bao'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Luowu campaign, Han Jiang had him serve as acting superintendent of Bao'an Army.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇順寧，思立擅領兵赴援，諸將敗，一軍獨全。

translations.literal: When the Xia raided Shunning, Sili on his own authority led troops to the relief; the other generals were defeated, but his command alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided Shunning, Sili on his own authority marched to the relief; the other generals were beaten, but his command alone came through intact.

sentences.zh: 以功知德順軍，策應王韶取熙州，過洮，築當川堡，克羌香子、珂諾城，遂定河州。

translations.literal: For this merit he was made prefect of Deshun Army. Supporting Wang Shao's capture of Xizhou, he crossed the Tao, built Dangchuan Fort, took the Qiang towns of Xiangzi and Kenuo, and thus secured Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made prefect of Deshun Army. Supporting Wang Shao's capture of Xizhou, he crossed the Tao, built Dangchuan Fort, took the Qiang towns of Xiangzi and Kenuo, and secured Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗與羌力戰，斬不用命者數人，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Once, fighting the Qiang in a fierce battle, he executed several who would not obey orders, and his army's reputation surged.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in a hard fight with the Qiang, he executed several men who would not obey orders, and his army's reputation surged.

sentences.zh: 韶言其臨事忠勇，進如京副使、通事舍人，再擢東上閣門使、河州刺史，賜繡旗、朱甲。

translations.literal: Shao reported his loyalty and courage in action. He was promoted to Vice Commissioner as If to the Capital and Drafter of Affairs, then again to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Hezhou, and was granted an embroidered banner and vermilion armor.
translations.idiomatic: Shao reported his loyalty and courage in action. He was promoted to Vice Commissioner as If to the Capital and Drafter of Affairs, then again to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Hezhou, and was granted an embroidered banner and vermilion armor.

sentences.zh: 又遷四方館使、河州團練使，知其州。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to Commissioner of the Hall of All Directions and regimental commissioner of Hezhou, and held the governorship of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was further transferred to Commissioner of the Hall of All Directions and regimental commissioner of Hezhou, and governed that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神宗知思立母老而未有官舍，命其弟思誼為秦州判官以便養。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong learned that Sili's mother was old and without an official residence, he appointed his younger brother Siyi as assistant prefect of Qinzhou to facilitate her care.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong learned that Sili's mother was old and had no official residence, he appointed his younger brother Siyi assistant prefect of Qinzhou so he could care for her.

sentences.zh: 青宜結鬼章舉兵襲殺伐木卒，害小校七人，以書抵思立，詞不遜。

translations.literal: Qingyijie Guizhang raised troops, attacked and killed woodcutting laborers, and killed seven low-ranking officers; he sent a letter to Sili in insolent terms.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyijie Guizhang raised troops, attacked and killed woodcutting laborers, and killed seven junior officers; he sent Sili a letter in insolent terms.

sentences.zh: 思立不能忍，帥兵六千攻之於踏白城。

translations.literal: Sili could not endure it and led six thousand men to attack him at Tabai Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Sili could not bear it and led six thousand men to attack him at Tabai Fort.

sentences.zh: 鈐轄韓存寶、蕃將瞎藥交止之，不聽。

translations.literal: Controllers Han Cunbao and the tribal general Xi Yaojiao tried to stop him; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Controllers Han Cunbao and the tribal general Xi Yaojiao tried to stop him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 自將中軍，使存寶及魏奇為先鋒，王存將左，賈翊將右。

translations.literal: He personally commanded the center army, made Cunbao and Wei Qi vanguard, Wang Cun the left wing, and Jia Yi the right.
translations.idiomatic: He personally commanded the center army, made Cunbao and Wei Qi vanguard, Wang Cun the left wing, and Jia Yi the right.

sentences.zh: 鬼章眾二萬，分三砦以抗官軍。

translations.literal: Guizhang's forces numbered twenty thousand; he split them among three forts to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhang had twenty thousand men and divided them among three forts to resist the government army.

sentences.zh: 戰數十合，羌從山下圍中軍。

translations.literal: After several dozen clashes, Qiang from the hills surrounded the center army.
translations.idiomatic: After several dozen engagements, Qiang from the hills surrounded the center army.

sentences.zh: 他將王寧、李元凱沒於陣，思立、存寶潰圍出，諸將多傷，議曰：「日暮兵疲，宜移屯東岡以自固。

translations.literal: Generals Wang Ning and Li Yuankai fell in the formation; Sili and Cunbao broke out of the encirclement. Many of the generals were wounded; they counseled: "It is evening and the troops are weary—we should shift camp to the eastern ridge to steady ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wang Ning and Li Yuankai fell in the battle; Sili and Cunbao broke out of the encirclement. Many of the generals were wounded, and they argued: "It is evening and the troops are exhausted—we should move camp to the eastern ridge and hold our ground."

sentences.zh: 」思立以魏奇創重，獨徙其軍，方遣之而殿後兵亂，前人望見，亦皆潰。

translations.literal: Sili, because Wei Qi was severely wounded, moved only his force alone. Just as he was dispatching them the rearguard fell into disorder; those ahead saw it and all fled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei Qi was badly wounded, Sili moved only his own force. Just as he was sending them off, the rearguard broke ranks; those in front saw it and fled as well.

sentences.zh: 思立且鬥且退，曰：「我適以百騎走羌數千人，無助我者，今敗矣，當自剄以謝朝廷。

translations.literal: Sili fought as he retreated and said: "A moment ago I drove off several thousand Qiang with a hundred horsemen, yet no one helped me. Now I am defeated—I should cut my own throat to atone to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Sili fought as he withdrew and said: "A moment ago I drove off several thousand Qiang with a hundred horsemen, and no one helped me. Now I am beaten—I ought to cut my own throat to answer to the court."

sentences.zh: 」眾止之。

translations.literal: The men restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: The men held him back.

sentences.zh: 少頃再戰，遂死。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he fought again and died.
translations.idiomatic: A little later he fought again and was killed.

sentences.zh: 時已除忠州防禦使，會其死，不及拜。

translations.literal: He had already been appointed defender of Zhongzhou, but he died before he could take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been appointed defender of Zhongzhou, but died before he could assume the post.

sentences.zh: 帝以其輕敵致敗，不復贈官。

translations.literal: Because he had treated the enemy lightly and brought on defeat, the Emperor did not posthumously grant him further rank.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had underestimated the enemy and brought on defeat, the Emperor did not posthumously grant him further rank.

sentences.zh: 王奇，汾州人，武舉中第。

translations.literal: Wang Qi was a native of Fenzhou and passed the military examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi came from Fenzhou and passed the military examination.

sentences.zh: 章惇經營湖北溪洞，以為將領，降其酋舒光貴，縛元猛，平懿、洽等州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun developed the stream-cave regions of Hubei, Qi served as a commander. He induced the chieftain Shu Guanggui to submit, bound Yuan Meng, and pacified Yi, Qia, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun developed the stream-cave regions of Hubei, Qi served as a commander. He induced the chieftain Shu Guanggui to submit, bound Yuan Meng, and pacified Yi, Qia, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 累遷如京副使，為湖南都監，徙廣西。

translations.literal: He rose through promotion to Vice Commissioner as If to the Capital, served as superintendent of Hunan, and was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through promotion to Vice Commissioner as If to the Capital, served as superintendent of Hunan, and was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 宜州蠻寇邊，奇領兵至天河縣，期旦日會戰。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of Yizhou raided the border, Qi led troops to Tianhe County and agreed to join battle at dawn the next day.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians of Yizhou raided the border, Qi led troops to Tianhe County and agreed to meet them in battle at dawn the next day.

sentences.zh: 裨將費萬夜以眾竊出河泥隘，戰沒。

translations.literal: Deputy general Fei Wan secretly led his force out by night through the Hemi Pass and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy general Fei Wan secretly led his men out by night through the Hemi Pass and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 經略使移書迫奇，奇不能堪。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner sent a letter pressing Qi; Qi could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner sent a letter pressing Qi, and Qi could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 後數日，蠻萬人驟集，奇輕出，遂敗。

translations.literal: Several days later ten thousand barbarians suddenly massed; Qi went out lightly guarded and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later ten thousand barbarians suddenly gathered; Qi went out with too few men and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 麾下猶數百人，勸策馬逃去，奇罵曰：「大丈夫當盡節以報國，何走為！

translations.literal: Several hundred men still remained under his command and urged him to spur his horse and flee. Qi cursed them: "A true man should die in full devotion for the state—why would I run?"
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred men still remained under his command and urged him to spur his horse and flee. Qi cursed them: "A true man should die in full devotion for the state—why would I run?"

sentences.zh: 」戰而死。

translations.literal: He fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on and was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈皇城使、忠州防禦使，官其家六人，仍賜金帛。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Inner Palatial Commissioner and defender of Zhongzhou, granted office to six members of his family, and still gave gold and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Inner Palatial Commissioner and defender of Zhongzhou, granted office to six members of his family, and also gave gold and cloth.

sentences.zh: 蔣興祖，常州宜興人，之奇之孫也。

translations.literal: Jiang Xingzu, a native of Yixing in Changzhou, was the grandson of Jiang Zhiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xingzu came from Yixing in Changzhou and was the grandson of Jiang Zhiqi.

sentences.zh: 以蔭累調饒州司錄。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he was repeatedly transferred until he served as registrar of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he was repeatedly transferred until he served as registrar of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 睦州盜起，旁郡皆震，興祖白州將糾吏卒，絹戰具，盜不敢謀。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Muzhou and neighboring prefectures were shaken, Xingzu reported to the prefect and mustered clerks and soldiers, supplied them with battle gear, and the bandits dared not scheme further.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Muzhou and neighboring prefectures were shaken, Xingzu reported to the prefect, mustered clerks and soldiers, and supplied them with battle gear, and the bandits dared not act.

sentences.zh: 以功遷官，知開封府陽武縣。

translations.literal: For this merit he was transferred in rank and made magistrate of Yangwu in Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was promoted and made magistrate of Yangwu in Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陽武，古博浪沙地，土脈脆惡，大河薄其南。

translations.literal: Yangwu stood on the ground of ancient Bolang Sand; the soil was brittle and poor, and the great river pressed upon its south.
translations.idiomatic: Yangwu stood on the ground of ancient Bolang Sand; the soil was brittle and poor, and the Yellow River pressed close on its south.

sentences.zh: 嘗積雨泛溢，埽且潰，興祖躬救護，露宿其上，彌四旬，堤以不壞。

translations.literal: Once after prolonged rain the waters rose and overflowed; the embankment was near collapse. Xingzu personally joined the rescue, slept in the open on it for forty days straight, and the dike held.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after prolonged rain, the waters rose and overflowed and the embankment was near collapse. Xingzu personally joined the rescue, slept in the open on the dike for forty days straight, and the levee held.

sentences.zh: 治為畿邑最，使者交薦之。

translations.literal: His governance ranked first among the capital-district counties, and envoys repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance ranked first among the capital-district counties, and envoys repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金兵犯京師，道過縣，或勸使走避，興祖曰：「吾世受國恩，當死於是。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when Jin troops assaulted the capital and passed through his county, some urged him to flee. Xingzu said: "My family has received the state's grace for generations—I ought to die right here."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when Jin troops assaulted the capital and passed through his county, some urged him to flee. Xingzu said: "My family has received the state's grace for generations—I ought to die right here."

sentences.zh: 」與妻子留不去。

translations.literal: He and his wife and children remained and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed with his wife and children and did not leave.

sentences.zh: 監兵與賊通，斬以徇。

translations.literal: A soldier supervising the watch had dealings with the enemy; Xingzu executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier supervising the watch had dealings with the enemy; Xingzu executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 金數百騎來攻，不勝，去。

translations.literal: Several hundred Jin horsemen came to attack but could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Jin horsemen came to attack but could not prevail and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日師益至，力不敵，死焉，年四十二。

translations.literal: The next day more troops arrived; unable to match their strength, he died there at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The next day more troops arrived; unable to match their strength, he was killed there at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 妻及長子相繼以悸死。

translations.literal: His wife and eldest son in succession died of shock.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and eldest son in turn died of shock.

sentences.zh: 詔贈朝散大夫。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Master of the Palace for Dispersion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Master of the Palace for Dispersion.

sentences.zh: 郭滸，德順中安堡人。

translations.literal: Guo Hu was a native of Zhong'an Fort in Deshun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hu came from Zhong'an Fort in Deshun.

sentences.zh: 從軍，積官至武經郎，為涇原第八副將。

translations.literal: He entered the army and through accumulated service rose to Gentleman for Military Classics, serving as eighth deputy commander in Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army and through accumulated service rose to Gentleman for Military Classics, serving as eighth deputy commander in Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 金人犯陝西，渭帥以下叛降，獨滸義不許，稱病去。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded Shaanxi, the commander of Weizhou and those below him rebelled and surrendered. Hu alone refused on grounds of righteousness and left, claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded Shaanxi, the commander of Weizhou and those below him rebelled and surrendered. Hu alone refused on grounds of righteousness and left, claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 帥惡忌之，傅致以罪，下之獄，脅使俱降。

translations.literal: The commander hated and envied him, piled on charges, and had him thrown into prison to coerce him into surrendering together with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The commander hated and envied him, piled on charges, and had him thrown into prison to coerce him into surrendering with the rest.

sentences.zh: 滸奮而呼曰：「大丈夫今得死所矣！

translations.literal: Hu cried out in ardor: "A true man has at last found the place to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu cried out in ardor: "A true man has at last found the place to die!"

sentences.zh: 終不能受汙。

translations.literal: [I] could in the end never accept defilement.
translations.idiomatic: I could never accept such dishonor.

sentences.zh: 叛逆大惡，天地所不容，吾雖死，誓不爾貸，當訴於地下耳。

translations.literal: Rebellion is a great evil that Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate. Though I die, I swear not to spare you—it shall be pleaded before the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion is a great evil that Heaven and Earth will not abide. Even in death I swear not to forgive you; I shall bring my grievance before the shades below.

sentences.zh: 」眾醜其語，即殺之。

translations.literal: " The crowd found his words repugnant and immediately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The men found his words repellent and immediately killed him.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，贈武翼大夫、忠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Martial Wing and prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianyan era, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Martial Wing and appointed prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 同死者朱友恭，西安人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yougong, who died with him, was a man of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong, who died with him, was a native of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 以忠翊郎為涇原第一副將。

translations.literal: As Lang for Loyal Support he served as First Assistant General of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As Lang for Loyal Support, he served as First Assistant General of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 部兵捍金人於華亭，數有功。

translations.literal: He led troops to resist the Jin at Huating and had merit on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against the Jin at Huating and won merit on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 會金兵大集，友恭赴敵力戰，為所得。

translations.literal: When Jin troops gathered in force, Yougong went to meet the enemy and fought fiercely but was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin forces massed, Yougong went out to meet the enemy and fought fiercely, but was captured.

sentences.zh: 渭帥既降，誘以甘言，許優進官秩，不肯從，更詆辱之。

translations.literal: After the Weizhou commander had surrendered, they tempted him with flattering words and promised him promotion in rank, but he refused to submit and they further reviled and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Weizhou commander had surrendered, the Jin tempted Yougong with flattering words and promised him promotion, but he refused. They then reviled and humiliated him further.

sentences.zh: 帥不勝忿，斷其脛以徇，經日乃斬之。

translations.literal: The commander, unable to contain his rage, severed his shins as a warning to others and beheaded him only after a full day had passed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander, beside himself with rage, severed Yougong's shins as a warning to the others and did not behead him until a full day had passed.

sentences.zh: 後贈敦武郎。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted the title Lang for Honest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title Lang for Honest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 吳革，字義夫，華州華陽人，國初勳臣廷祚七世孫也。

translations.literal: Wu Ge, style name Yifu, was a man of Huayang in Huazhou, a seventh-generation descendant of the early-dynasty meritorious minister Tingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ge, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Huayang in Huazhou and a seventh-generation descendant of the founding-era meritorious minister Tingzuo.

sentences.zh: 少好學，喜談兵。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and delighted in discussing military matters.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning and delighted in discussing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 再試禮部不中，乃從涇原軍，以秉義郎幹辦經略司公事。

translations.literal: After failing the Ministry of Rites examination twice, he joined the Jingyuan army and served as Lang for Holding Righteousness, handling affairs for the frontier commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the Ministry of Rites examination twice, he joined the Jingyuan army as Lang for Holding Righteousness, handling business for the frontier commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 金人南牧，帥兵解遼州之圍。

translations.literal: When the Jin drove south, he commanded troops and lifted the siege of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin drove south, he led troops and lifted the siege of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 使粘罕軍，見之庭，揖不拜，責其貪利敗約，詞直氣勁。

translations.literal: Sent to Nianhan's camp, he was received in the court. He bowed with clasped hands but did not prostrate himself, reproaching them for coveting gain and breaking the treaty—his words were direct and his spirit forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Nianhan's camp, he was received in the court. He clasped his hands in salute but did not prostrate himself, accusing the Jin of coveting gain and breaking their treaty. His words were blunt and his bearing forceful.

sentences.zh: 粘罕少屈，為追回威勝諸屯兵，授書使歸。

translations.literal: Nianhan yielded somewhat; he had the garrison troops of Weisheng and elsewhere recalled and gave him a letter to take back.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan yielded slightly, recalled the garrison troops at Weisheng and elsewhere, and gave him a letter to carry home.

sentences.zh: 欽宗問割地與不割地利害，對曰：「金人有吞噬之意，願悉起關中士馬赴都為備。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong asked about the advantages and disadvantages of ceding territory or not; he replied: "The Jin intend to devour us. I wish to raise all the soldiers and horses of Guanzhong and send them to the capital for defense."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong asked about the pros and cons of ceding territory, he replied: "The Jin mean to devour us. I urge that all the troops and horses of Guanzhong be mobilized and sent to the capital to prepare the defense."

sentences.zh: 」詔以為武功大夫、閣門宣讚舍人，持節諭陝西。

translations.literal: " An edict appointed him Grand Master of Martial Achievement, Gate Proclamation Attendant, and bearer of credentials to proclaim this in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Grand Master of Martial Achievement and Gate Proclamation Attendant, sending him with imperial credentials to proclaim this in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 行至朱遷，聞金人犯京師，復還。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhuyan, he heard that the Jin were attacking the capital and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhuyan, he heard that the Jin were attacking the capital and returned at once.

sentences.zh: 與張叔夜同入城，請於帝，乞幸秦州；

translations.literal: He entered the city together with Zhang Shuye, pleaded with the emperor, and begged that he take refuge in Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He entered the city with Zhang Shuye, pleaded before the emperor, and begged him to withdraw to Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 又乞出城劫之，使不敢近；

translations.literal: he also begged to lead raids out of the city to harry them and keep them from approaching;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked permission to lead raiding parties out of the city to harry the enemy and keep them from closing in;

sentences.zh: 又乞諸門同出兵牽制、衝突、尾襲、應援，可一戰而勝。

translations.literal: and further begged that all the gates send out troops together to pin the enemy down, strike them head-on, attack from the rear, and support one another—a single battle could bring victory.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that troops be sent out together from every gate to pin the enemy down, strike them in front, harry them from the rear, and support one another, so that victory might be won in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 時眾言已入，皆不果。

translations.literal: By then many other proposals had already been adopted, and none of his were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: By then other counsels had already prevailed, and none of his plans were adopted.

sentences.zh: 後金兵攻安上門，填道度壕，革言之守將，使泄蔡河水以灌之，不聽。

translations.literal: Later, when Jin troops attacked the Anshang Gate and were filling the road and crossing the moat, Ge told the defending general to release the Cai River water to flood them, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jin troops attacked the Anshang Gate and began filling in the road and crossing the moat, Ge urged the defending general to release the waters of the Cai River to flood them, but the general would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及填道將合，欲用前議，則水已涸矣。

translations.literal: When the filled road was nearly complete and they wished to use his earlier plan, the water had already dried up.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the filled road was almost complete and they wished to adopt his earlier plan, the water had already run dry.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸金營，革以為墮其詐，往請叔夜，欲身見其大酋計事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to the Jin camp, Ge believed this was falling into their deception. He went to request Zhang Shuye and wished to see their chief commander in person to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage was sent to the Jin camp, Ge believed the court had fallen into their trap. He went to Zhang Shuye and asked to see the Jin chief commander in person to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 叔夜問其故，曰：「茲行有三說：一則天子還內，二則金騎歸國，三則革死。

translations.literal: Shuye asked his reason; he said: "This journey has three possible outcomes: the Son of Heaven returns within the walls; the Jin cavalry go home; or Ge dies."
translations.idiomatic: Shuye asked why. He said: "This journey has three possible outcomes: the emperor returns inside the walls, the Jin cavalry withdraw, or I die."

sentences.zh: 」叔夜為言之，不報。

translations.literal: " Shuye relayed this on his behalf, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye relayed this to the court, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 上皇、妃、後、太子出郊，革白孫傅乞留之，不得。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor, consorts, empress, and crown prince went out to the suburbs, Ge told Sun Fu and begged that they be kept back, but he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor, consorts, empress, and crown prince went out to meet the enemy in the suburbs, Ge appealed to Sun Fu to hold them back, but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 乃為傅謀，於啟聖僧院置振濟局，募士民就食。

translations.literal: He then devised a plan for Fu: at the Qisheng Monastery they established a relief office and recruited commoners and soldiers to come for food.
translations.idiomatic: He then devised a plan for Sun Fu: at the Qisheng Monastery they set up a relief office and summoned townspeople and soldiers to come for rations.

sentences.zh: 一日之間至者萬計，陰以軍法部勒，將攻金營。

translations.literal: Within a single day tens of thousands arrived; secretly he disciplined them by military law, intending to attack the Jin camp.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day tens of thousands had gathered. Secretly he drilled them under military law, preparing to attack the Jin camp.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷於同文館，所合已至數萬，多兩河驍悍之士。

translations.literal: After some time they moved to the Tongwen Hall; those assembled had already reached tens of thousands, many of them fierce warriors from the Two He regions.
translations.idiomatic: After some time they moved to the Tongwen Hall. Those gathered now numbered in the tens of thousands, many of them fierce warriors from the Two He regions.

sentences.zh: 既而有立張邦昌之議，革謀先誅範瓊輩，以三月八日起兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward there arose talk of enthroning Zhang Bangchang; Ge planned first to execute Fan Qiong and his faction and to raise troops on the eighth day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: Before long talk arose of enthroning Zhang Bangchang. Ge planned to execute Fan Qiong and his faction first and to raise troops on the eighth day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 謀既定，前期二日，有班直甲士數百人排闥入言：「邦昌以七日受冊，請亟起事。

translations.literal: Once the plan was settled, two days before the date several hundred armored palace guards burst in and said: "Bangchang is to receive investiture on the seventh—please rise at once."
translations.idiomatic: Two days before the planned date, several hundred armored palace guards burst in and said: "Bangchang is to be enthroned on the seventh. You must act immediately."

sentences.zh: 」革乃被甲上馬，至咸豐門，四面皆瓊黨，紿革入帳，即執之，脅以從逆。

translations.literal: " Ge then donned armor, mounted a horse, and went to the Xianfeng Gate. On every side were Qiong's partisans; they tricked Ge into entering a tent, seized him at once, and coerced him to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ge donned armor, mounted, and rode to the Xianfeng Gate. Qiong's partisans were on every side. They lured him into a tent, seized him at once, and tried to force him to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 革罵之極口，引頸受刃，顏色不變。

translations.literal: Ge cursed them with the utmost vehemence, stretched out his neck to receive the blade, and his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Ge cursed them with every breath, bared his neck to the blade, and did not change expression.

sentences.zh: 其麾下百人皆同死。

translations.literal: The hundred men under his command all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred men under his command all died with him.

sentences.zh: 李翼，麟州新秦人。

translations.literal: Li Yi was a man of Xinqin in Linzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was a native of Xinqin in Linzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，為代州西路都巡檢使，屯崞縣。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era he served as West Route Frontier Inspector of Daizhou, stationed at Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era he served as West Route Frontier Inspector of Daizhou and was stationed at Guo County.

sentences.zh: 金人取代，執守將嗣本，遣來諭降，翼射卻之，帥士卒堅守。

translations.literal: When the Jin took Daizhou they seized the defending general Siben, sent him to urge surrender; Yi drove him off with arrows and led his soldiers in a stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin captured Daizhou they seized the defending general Siben and sent him to urge surrender. Yi drove him off with arrows and led his soldiers in a resolute defense.

sentences.zh: 義勝軍統領崔忠殺都監張洪輔，夜引金兵入城，翼挺身搏戰達旦，力不敵被執。

translations.literal: Cui Zhong, commander of the Yisheng Army, killed Frontier Supervisor Zhang Hongfu and by night brought Jin troops into the city. Yi fought hand to hand until dawn; overpowered, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhong, commander of the Yisheng Army, killed the frontier supervisor Zhang Hongfu and by night brought Jin troops into the city. Yi fought hand to hand until dawn, but was overpowered and captured.

sentences.zh: 酋粘罕欲臣之，怒罵不屈，與縣令李聳、丞王唐臣、尉劉子英、監酒閻誠、將官折可與同死之。

translations.literal: The chieftain Nianhan wished to make him submit; cursing angrily, he would not yield. Together with Magistrate Li Song, Assistant Magistrate Wang Tangchen, District Captain Liu Ziying, Wine Supervisor Yan Cheng, and officer Zhe Keyu, he died with them.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Nianhan wished to make him submit, but Yi cursed him and would not yield. He was killed together with Magistrate Li Song, Assistant Magistrate Wang Tangchen, District Captain Liu Ziying, Wine Supervisor Yan Cheng, and the officer Zhe Keyu.

sentences.zh: 阮駿者，興化軍人。

translations.literal: Ruan Jun was a man of Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Jun was a native of Xinghua Army.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年進士，為河南府少尹。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Shaosheng, he served as Vice Director of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the first year of Shaosheng, he served as Vice Director of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，率所隸兵擁護神御殿，抱神御，罵聲不絕口，卒被害。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked the capital, he led the troops under his command to protect the Hall of Imperial Portraits, clasped the imperial portraits, and cursed without cease until he was killed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked the capital, he led the troops under his command to protect the Hall of Imperial Portraits, clasped the imperial portraits in his arms, and cursed the enemy without cease until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 特贈朝議大夫。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously granted the title of Grand Master for Discussion at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Discussion at Court.

sentences.zh: 趙士嶐字景瞻，太宗之後。

translations.literal: Zhao Shilong, style name Jingzhan, was a descendant of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shilong, courtesy name Jingzhan, was a descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 生五歲，補右班殿直。

translations.literal: At five years of age he was given the post of Right Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of five he was appointed Right Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 既長，遊庠序，月試數居前列。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied at the academy; in monthly examinations he often ranked among the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied at the local academy and often ranked among the top in the monthly examinations.

sentences.zh: 一日，投筆歎曰：「昔賢有不願為章句儒，出玉門關、佩侯印者，彼何人哉！

translations.literal: One day he cast down his brush and sighed, saying: "Ancient worthies who refused to be pedantic scholars of passages and phrases, who went out beyond Jade Gate Pass and wore a marquis's seal—what sort of men were they!"
translations.idiomatic: One day he threw down his brush and sighed: "There were worthies of old who scorned to be pedantic scholars of passages and phrases, who went beyond Jade Gate Pass and wore a marquis's seal—what sort of men were they!"

sentences.zh: 」遂不復事科舉。

translations.literal: " He then no longer pursued the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He never pursued the civil examinations again.

sentences.zh: 去為郡縣吏，累遷至淮南西路兵馬鈐轄，駐壽春。

translations.literal: He left to serve as a county and prefectural official, rose by stages to Military Controller of Huainan West Route, and was stationed at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He left to serve as a county and prefectural official, rose by stages to Military Controller of Huainan West Route, and was stationed at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 劇賊丁一箭眾號十萬，來攻城。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Ding Yijian, whom his followers numbered at one hundred thousand, came to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce bandit Ding Yijian, whose followers were said to number one hundred thousand, came to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 郡守不知兵，凡備禦之策悉委士嶐。

translations.literal: The prefect knew nothing of warfare; all measures of defense he entrusted entirely to Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect knew nothing of warfare and entrusted all defensive measures entirely to Shilong.

sentences.zh: 賊三旬不退，士嶐募軍中敢死士與之謀。

translations.literal: The bandits did not withdraw for thirty days; Shilong recruited dare-to-die men in the army to plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did not withdraw for thirty days. Shilong recruited dare-to-die fighters from the army to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 有張宣者應募，獨持槊縋城下，擊殺數十人，賊眾披靡。

translations.literal: One Zhang Xuan answered the call; alone he held a spear, lowered himself by rope below the wall, struck down several dozen men, and the bandit horde broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhang Xuan answered the call. Alone, spear in hand, he was lowered by rope below the wall, killed several dozen men, and put the bandits to flight.

sentences.zh: 乃選壯士數百人夜開城門，出其不意擊走之，追奔數十里。

translations.literal: He then chose several hundred stalwart men, opened the city gates by night, struck them by surprise and drove them off, and pursued the rout for several dozen li.
translations.idiomatic: He then chose several hundred stalwart fighters, opened the city gates by night, took the enemy by surprise and drove them off, and pursued them for several dozen li.

sentences.zh: 以功遷三官，秩滿，授江東路鈐轄。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted three ranks; when his term expired he was appointed Military Controller of Jiangdong Route.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted three ranks. When his term expired he was appointed Military Controller of Jiangdong Route.

sentences.zh: 李成叛，據江、淮六七郡，連兵數萬，遣其黨馬進圍九江，守臣姚舜明與士嶐及副鈐轄劉紹先禦之。

translations.literal: Li Cheng rebelled, held six or seven prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai, and mustered tens of thousands of troops; he sent his follower Ma Jin to besiege Jiujiang. The defending official Yao Shunming, together with Shilong and Vice Controller Liu Shaoxian, resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng rebelled and held six or seven prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai with a force of tens of thousands. He sent his follower Ma Jin to besiege Jiujiang. The defending official Yao Shunming, together with Shilong and Vice Controller Liu Shaoxian, held them off.

sentences.zh: 進攻城益急，士嶐竭力捍守。

translations.literal: Ma Jin pressed the siege ever harder, and Shilong exerted all his strength to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jin pressed the siege ever harder, and Shilong defended the city with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 江東帥呂頤浩屯鄱陽，既復南康，與建武節度使楊惟忠兵會，遣統製巨師古援江州，未至，遇伏敗。

translations.literal: The Jiangdong commander Lu Yihao was encamped at Poyang; having recovered Nankang, he joined forces with the Jianwu Military Commissioner Yang Weizhong and dispatched Commissioner-in-Chief Ju Shigu to relieve Jiangzhou, but before arriving he was ambushed and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdong commander Lu Yihao was encamped at Poyang. After recovering Nankang, he joined forces with Jianwu Military Commissioner Yang Weizhong and sent Commissioner-in-Chief Ju Shigu to relieve Jiangzhou, but Ju was ambushed and defeated before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年正月，詔張俊為江、淮招討使，入辭，頗言成兵眾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shaoxing, Zhang Jun was ordered to serve as Jiang-Huai Pacification Commissioner. When he took leave to depart he spoke at length about the size of Li Cheng's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Shaoxing, Zhang Jun was appointed Jiang-Huai Pacification Commissioner. When he took leave before departing, he spoke at length about the size of Li Cheng's force.

sentences.zh: 高宗責以立功，俊悚懼受命。

translations.literal: Gaozong rebuked him and ordered him to achieve merit; Jun, fear-stricken, accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong rebuked him and ordered him to win merit. Jun, awed and fearful, accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 未至，城已陷。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, the city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, the city had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 時守城罷卒僅數千，捍賊百餘日，城中食盡。

translations.literal: At the time there were only a few thousand exhausted troops holding the city; they had resisted the bandits for more than a hundred days, and provisions in the city were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: By then only a few thousand exhausted troops remained in the city. They had held off the bandits for more than a hundred days, and food inside the walls was gone.

sentences.zh: 舜明、紹先議縱火，因棄城去，士嶐毅然獨糾合部曲餘民守城。

translations.literal: Shunming and Shaoxian debated setting fires and abandoning the city to flee; Shilong resolutely alone rallied his company and the remaining people to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shunming and Shaoxian planned to set fires and abandon the city, but Shilong resolutely rallied his company and the remaining townspeople to keep defending.

sentences.zh: 城破，眾號呼曰：「無殺我趙鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the crowd cried out: "Do not kill our Controller Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the people cried out: "Do not kill our Controller Zhao!"

sentences.zh: 」賊入城大掠。

translations.literal: " The bandits entered the city and plundered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits entered the city and plundered it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 成素服士嶐之義，欲以為偽安撫使，士嶐怒罵曰：「賊欲屈我耶！

translations.literal: Li Cheng had long admired Shilong's integrity and wished to make him a puppet Pacification Commissioner; Shilong cursed in rage, saying: "Do the bandits think they can break me!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng had long admired Shilong's integrity and wished to make him a puppet Pacification Commissioner. Shilong cursed: "Do you bandits think you can break me!"

sentences.zh: 」陰裂帛以書使示諸子曰：「賊不殺我，義不苟活，汝輩得出，為我雪恥。

translations.literal: " Secretly he tore silk and wrote a message to show his sons: "If the bandits do not kill me, on principle I cannot live dishonorably. You may get out—avenge my shame for me."
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he tore silk and wrote a message for his sons: "If the bandits do not kill me, I cannot live dishonorably. You may escape. Avenge my shame for me."

sentences.zh: 」遂仰藥而卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: " He then drank poison and died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He then swallowed poison and died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，並害其家數十口。

translations.literal: The bandits in rage killed his entire family—several dozen people.
translations.idiomatic: In rage the bandits killed his entire family, dozens of people in all.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上嘉悼，贈武功大夫，官其孫二人。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the emperor praised and mourned him, posthumously granted him Grand Master of Martial Achievement, and gave offices to two of his grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, the emperor praised and mourned him, posthumously granted him the title Grand Master of Martial Achievement, and gave offices to two of his grandsons.

sentences.zh: 士嶐六子，皆有文行：不惉、不{乂心}、不愆、不恧、不{滯心}、不隱。

translations.literal: Shilong had six sons, all accomplished in letters and conduct: Bu Ti, Bu {乂心}, Bu Qian, Bu Nu, Bu {滯心}, and Bu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had six sons, all accomplished in letters and conduct: Bu Ti, Bu Yi, Bu Qian, Bu Nu, Bu Zhi, and Bu Yin.

sentences.zh: 是役也，不{乂心}、不{滯心}、不隱死焉。

translations.literal: In this campaign, Bu {乂心}, Bu {滯心}, and Bu Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Bu Yi, Bu Zhi, and Bu Yin were killed.

sentences.zh: 又宗子有士醫、士真、士遒，皆以死事聞。

translations.literal: Among imperial clansmen there were also Shiyi, Shizhen, and Shiqiu, all famed for dying in service.
translations.idiomatic: Among other clansmen were Shiyi, Shizhen, and Shiqiu, all renowned for dying in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 士醫，任秀州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Shiyi served as Military Supervisor of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi served as Military Supervisor of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，兀术入州，士醫乘城拒戰，城陷死之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, Wuzhu entered the prefecture; Shiyi fought from the walls in resistance, and when the city fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyan, Wuzhu entered the prefecture. Shiyi fought from the walls, and when the city fell he was killed.

sentences.zh: 後贈武翼大夫，官其二子。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Martial Wing, and two of his sons received offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Martial Wing, and two of his sons were given offices.

sentences.zh: 士真，權知信陽軍。

translations.literal: Shizhen served as acting prefect of Xinyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen served as acting prefect of Xinyang Army.

sentences.zh: 寇劉滿至，士真拒之。

translations.literal: When the bandit Liu Man arrived, Shizhen resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Liu Man arrived, Shizhen held him off.

sentences.zh: 兵潰，滿執之去荊門，遇害。

translations.literal: The troops broke; Man seized him and took him away to Jingmen, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops broke. Liu Man seized him and took him to Jingmen, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 後贈右朝奉大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Right Grand Master for Attending Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title Right Grand Master for Attending Court.

sentences.zh: 官其一子。

translations.literal: One of his sons received an office.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was given an office.

sentences.zh: 士遒，以武翼大夫守官江州。

translations.literal: Shiqiu, as Grand Master of Martial Wing, held office at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqiu held office at Jiangzhou with the rank of Grand Master of Martial Wing.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，馬進寇江州，士遒遇害。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Ma Jin raided Jiangzhou, and Shiqiu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Ma Jin attacked Jiangzhou, and Shiqiu was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈武德大夫，官其家二人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Martial Virtue, and two members of his family received offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Martial Virtue, and two members of his family were given offices.

sentences.zh: 士跂，濮王曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shiqi was a great-grandson of Prince Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was a great-grandson of Prince Pu.

sentences.zh: 靖康末，為右監門衛大將軍、吉州團練使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingkang he served as Grand General of the Right Gate-guard Corps and Military Commissioner of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingkang era he served as Grand General of the Right Gate-guard Corps and Military Commissioner of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人驅宗室北行，士跂得間道遁去。

translations.literal: When the Jin drove the imperial clansmen north, Shiqi escaped by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin drove the imperial clansmen north, Shiqi fled by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 居邢州，結土豪將舉事。

translations.literal: Living in Xingzhou, he joined with local strongmen and planned to raise an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Xingzhou, rallied local strongmen, and planned an uprising.

sentences.zh: 有告者，金人執而殺之。

translations.literal: There was an informer; the Jin seized him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed on him, and the Jin seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈保寧軍節度使，諡忠果。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Military Commissioner of Baoning Army and given the posthumous name Zhongguo (Loyal and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted the title Military Commissioner of Baoning Army and given the posthumous name Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 叔皎，秦悼王四世孫。

translations.literal: Shujiao was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Daizhao of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shujiao was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Daizhao of Qin.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，為右班殿直，累遷至德州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era he served as Right Guard Attendant and rose by stages to Military Supervisor of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era he served as Right Guard Attendant and rose by stages to Military Supervisor of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 自靖康以來，劉順、呂拱、劉亨相繼謀叛，叔皎皆設方略捕擒之。

translations.literal: From Jingkang onward, Liu Shun, Lu Gong, and Liu Heng plotted rebellion in succession; Shujiao each time devised plans and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingkang era onward, Liu Shun, Lu Gong, and Liu Heng plotted rebellion in turn. Each time Shujiao devised plans and captured them.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人圍城，郡檄叔皎率兵禦之，前後六戰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan the Jin besieged the city; the prefecture ordered Shujiao to lead troops in defense, and he fought six battles before and after.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan the Jin besieged the city. The prefecture ordered Shujiao to lead troops in defense, and he fought six battles in all.

sentences.zh: 圍急，有江喆者，與郡守宗諒謀以城降，叔皎斬喆以徇。

translations.literal: When the siege grew pressing, one Jiang Zhe, together with the prefect Zong Liang, plotted to surrender the city; Shujiao beheaded Zhe as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, a man named Jiang Zhe plotted with the prefect Zong Liang to surrender the city. Shujiao beheaded Jiang Zhe as a warning.

sentences.zh: 金人登城，叔皎猶力戰，勢窮被執，怒罵不屈，遂遇害。

translations.literal: When the Jin scaled the wall, Shujiao still fought fiercely; his strength exhausted, he was seized, cursed them in rage and would not yield, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin scaled the walls, Shujiao still fought fiercely. His strength exhausted, he was captured. He cursed them and would not yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 叔憑，建炎間，任陝州都監，累官武翼大夫，就遷通守。

translations.literal: Shu Ping, during the Jianyan period, served as Director-General of Shaanzhou, rose through the ranks to Grand Master of Martial Feathers, and was then promoted to General Defender.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era, Shu Ping served as military commandant of Shaanzhou, advanced through the ranks to Grand Master of Martial Feathers, and was subsequently promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 金人圍陝州既久，援兵不至，城危。

translations.literal: The Jurchens had besieged Shaanzhou for a long time; relief troops did not arrive; the city was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens had besieged Shaanzhou for a long time, but no relief force came, and the city stood in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 時叔憑子官盧氏，遺以蠟丸書曰：「人臣當死國難，況吾以近屬，其可辱命耶？

translations.literal: At the time Shu Ping's son held office in Lushi; he sent him a letter in a wax-sealed pellet, saying: "As a minister one ought to die in the nation's crisis—how much more so I, being a close kinsman of the throne—could I disgrace my charge?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu Ping's son was then serving as an official in Lushi County. Shu Ping sent him a letter concealed in a wax pellet: "A subject should die for his country in times of national crisis—and I, as a close member of the imperial clan, how could I fail in my duty?"

sentences.zh: 死固其所也。

translations.literal: Death is indeed what is proper.
translations.idiomatic: Death is only what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」遂死之。

translations.literal: He thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon met his death.

sentences.zh: 時通判王滸，職官劉效、陳思道、馮經、李嶽、杜開，縣令張玘，將佐盧亨等五十一人俱死，無降者。

translations.literal: At the time the Vice-Prefect Wang Hu, the officials Liu Xiao, Chen Sidao, Feng Jing, Li Yue, and Du Kai, the Magistrate Zhang Qi, the commander Lu Heng, and fifty-one others in all died; there were none who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Prefect Wang Hu, staff officers Liu Xiao, Chen Sidao, Feng Jing, Li Yue, and Du Kai, Magistrate Zhang Qi, Commander Lu Heng, and forty-eight others—all fifty-one in total—died with him; not one surrendered.

sentences.zh: 訓之字誨道，秦悼王五世孫。

translations.literal: Xun Zhi, courtesy name Huidao, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Daozhong of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhi, style name Huidao, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Daozhong of Qin.

sentences.zh: 父叔侯，官至惠州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Shu Hou reached the office of Defense Commissioner of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Shu Hou, rose to the rank of Defense Commissioner of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 訓之登政和二年進士，調東平儀曹，知平江府吳縣。

translations.literal: Xun Zhi passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenghe, was assigned to the Ceremonial Office of Dongping, and served as magistrate of Wuxian in Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhi passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Zhenghe reign and was appointed to the ceremonial office at Dongping before becoming magistrate of Wuxian in Pingjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱勔怙勢役州縣，訓之不為屈。

translations.literal: Zhu Mi relied on his influence to press the prefectures and counties; Xun Zhi would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mi abused his power to coerce prefectures and counties, but Xun Zhi refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 勔嘗執數輩詣縣請治，訓之悉縱之。

translations.literal: Mi once seized several men and brought them to the county to be punished; Xun Zhi released them all.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Mi seized several men and brought them to the county seat to be punished, but Xun Zhi released them all.

sentences.zh: 懺勔，遂移疾去。

translations.literal: Fearing Mi, he soon tendered his resignation on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wary of Mi's retaliation, he soon resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，盜起河北，訓之屢與人言：「契丹舊盟未可渝，金人新好未可恃。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era, bandits rose in Hebei; Xun Zhi repeatedly told others: "The old alliance with the Khitans must not be violated; the new friendship with the Jurchens must not be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xuanhe reign, bandits rose in Hebei, and Xun Zhi repeatedly warned those around him: "The old alliance with the Khitans must not be cast aside, and the new friendship with the Jurchens must not be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，金人犯京師，訓之居揚州，率大姓募士勤王，聞都城失守，乃止。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens invaded the capital; Xun Zhi was living in Yangzhou and led the great clans in recruiting men to rescue the throne, but when he heard that the capital had fallen he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jurchens attacked the capital. Xun Zhi was then living in Yangzhou and rallied the leading families to recruit troops to rescue the throne, but when he learned that the capital had fallen, he ceased the effort.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，知吉州永豐縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, he served as magistrate of Yongfeng County in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, he was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng County in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 孟太后避地虔州，護衛統製杜彥與其麾下叛，後軍楊世雄應之，將犯永豐。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Meng took refuge in Qianzhou, Du Yan, the commander of the escort guard, rebelled with his troops, and Yang Shixiong of the rear guard responded; they were about to attack Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Meng fled to Qianzhou, Du Yan, commander of the imperial escort, rebelled with his troops, and Yang Shixiong of the rear guard joined him; together they were about to attack Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 訓之與尉陳自仁簡兵分為二，一取間道繞賊後，一據地利匿其精兵以誘賊。

translations.literal: Xun Zhi and the sheriff Chen Ziren selected troops and divided them in two: one force took a hidden route to circle behind the rebels, the other seized favorable ground and concealed its elite troops to lure the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhi and Sheriff Chen Ziren picked their troops and split them into two forces: one took a hidden route to strike the rebels from behind, while the other seized advantageous ground, concealed its best soldiers, and used them as bait.

sentences.zh: 賊至伏發，殲其眾。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived the ambush was sprung and their force was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the ambush was sprung and their force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 會賊別校繼至，官兵未成列，訓之率數十輩拒戰，厲聲罵賊，與自仁俱被害。

translations.literal: Just then another rebel detachment arrived; the government troops had not yet formed ranks; Xun Zhi led several dozen men to resist, cursing the rebels loudly, and he and Ziren were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then another rebel detachment arrived before the government troops had formed ranks. Xun Zhi led several dozen men into the fight, cursing the rebels at the top of his voice, and both he and Ziren were killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔贈訓之朝散郎、直秘閣，諡忠果，自仁通直郎，官其子，邑人為立祠。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, an edict posthumously awarded Xun Zhi the rank of Gentleman for Dispersing Morals and appointment to the Secretariat Pavilion, with the posthumous title Zhongguo; Ziren received the rank of Vice Director of the Palace Library; their sons were given office, and the people of the district built a shrine for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, an edict posthumously granted Xun Zhi the rank of Gentleman for Dispersing Morals and appointment to the Secretariat Pavilion, with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute; Ziren was granted Vice Director of the Palace Library; their sons were given official posts; and the local people built a shrine in their honor.

sentences.zh: 太后之發吉州也，至太和，眾皆潰。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager set out from Jizhou and reached Taihe, the whole force scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager departed Jizhou and reached Taihe, her entire escort disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 從事郎、三省樞密院幹辦官劉德老為金人追騎所殺。

translations.literal: Liu Delao, Attendant Gentleman and staff officer of the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs, was killed by Jurchen pursuit cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Delao, an Attendant Gentleman and staff officer of the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs, was killed by Jurchen pursuit cavalry.

sentences.zh: 官其家一人。

translations.literal: One member of his family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: One member of his family was granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 是年，金人過江，陳淬戰死，岳飛等兵皆引去。

translations.literal: That year the Jurchens crossed the Yangtze; Chen Cui died in battle, and the armies of Yue Fei and others all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Jurchens crossed the Yangtze. Chen Cui died in battle, and the armies of Yue Fei and others all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上元丞趙壘之帥鄉兵迎敵，死之。

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate Zhao Leizhi of Shangyuan led local militia to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Leizhi, assistant magistrate of Shangyuan, led local militia to meet the enemy and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈奉議郎，官其家一人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Gentleman for Counselling and one member of his family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman for Counselling, and one member of his family received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 聿之，安定郡王叔東子也。

translations.literal: Yu Zhi was the son of Prince Anding's heir Shu Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhi was the son of Shu Dong, heir to Prince Anding.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，為成忠郎。

translations.literal: During Jianyan he served as Gentleman for Loyalty and Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan period he held the rank of Gentleman for Loyalty and Integrity.

sentences.zh: 金人圍潭州，帥臣向子諲率眾守城，聿之隸東壁。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens besieged Tanzhou, the commander Xiang Ziyin led the people in defending the city; Yu Zhi was assigned to the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged Tanzhou, the commander Xiang Ziyin led the defense of the city, and Yu Zhi was posted to the eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 子諲循城，顧聿之曰：「君宗室，不可效他人苟簡。

translations.literal: Ziyin made the rounds of the wall and, seeing Yu Zhi, said: "You are of the imperial clan—you must not follow others in taking things lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyin made the rounds of the wall and, turning to Yu Zhi, said, "You are of the imperial clan—you must not behave as others do and treat this lightly."

sentences.zh: 」聿之感慨流涕。

translations.literal: Yu Zhi was moved and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhi was deeply moved and wept.

sentences.zh: 金兵登城縱火，子諲率官吏突門遁去，城遂陷，聿之巷戰，大罵而死。

translations.literal: The Jurchen troops scaled the wall and set fires; Ziyin led the officials and clerks to burst through a gate and flee; the city then fell; Yu Zhi fought in the lanes, cursing loudly until he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen troops scaled the wall and set fires. Ziyin led the officials and clerks in a breakout through the gate and fled, and the city fell. Yu Zhi fought street by street, cursing the enemy until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 將官武經郎劉玠亦死之。

translations.literal: The officer Military Gentleman Liu Qi also died.
translations.idiomatic: The officer Liu Qi, a Military Gentleman, also died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈聿之左監門衛大將軍，玠武經大夫，皆官其家。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Yu Zhi was posthumously awarded Left Grand General of the Gate Guard, and Qi Military Grand Master; both their families were given office.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Yu Zhi was posthumously granted the rank of Left Grand General of the Gate Guard and Qi that of Military Grand Master; members of both their families received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 其後朱熹為請立廟，賜號忠節。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Xi petitioned to establish a temple for him, and the title Zhongjie was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Xi petitioned to have a temple erected in his honor, and the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast was granted.

sentences.zh: 陳淬，字君銳，興化軍莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Cui, courtesy name Junrui, was a native of Putian in Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Cui, style name Junrui, was a native of Putian in Xinghua Circuit.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，下第，挾策西遊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he failed the examinations and traveled west with his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng reign he failed the civil examinations and set out westward with his writings in hand.

sentences.zh: 時呂惠卿帥鄜延，淬戎服往見，惠卿問相見何事，淬曰：「大丈夫求見大丈夫，又何事？

translations.literal: At the time Lü Huiqing commanded Yan-Yan; Cui went to see him in military dress; Huiqing asked what business brought him; Cui said: "A great man seeks a great man—what business is there?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Huiqing was commanding the Yan-Yan frontier. Cui went to see him dressed for war. Huiqing asked what brought him, and Cui replied, "A great man comes to seek a great man—what other business could there be?"

sentences.zh: 」惠卿器之，補三班奉職。

translations.literal: Huiqing admired him and appointed him to Third-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing was impressed and appointed him Third-Rank Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與西人接戰於烏原，手殺十餘人，擒其砦主。

translations.literal: He joined battle with the western tribes at Wuyuan, personally killed more than ten men, and captured the fort commander.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the western tribes at Wuyuan, personally killed more than ten men, and captured the fort commander.

sentences.zh: 奏為左班殿直、鄜延路兵馬都監，累遷武經郎。

translations.literal: He was memorialized as Left-Rank Palace Attendant and Director-General of Yan-Yan Route troops, and was promoted through the ranks to Military Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended for appointment as Left-Rank Palace Attendant and Director-General of troops on the Yan-Yan Route, and rose through the ranks to Military Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，召赴闕，授真定路分都監兼知北砦、河北第一將，尋拜忠州團練使、真定府路馬步副總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe he was summoned to court, appointed Deputy Director-General of Zhending Route and concurrently magistrate of the Northern Fort, and soon after made Regimental Commander of Zhongzhou and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Zhending Prefecture horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe he was summoned to court, appointed deputy director-general of the Zhending Route and concurrently magistrate of the northern fort, and soon after made regimental commander of Zhongzhou and deputy commander-in-chief of the Zhending Prefecture horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 七年，金人入真定，淬以孤軍禦之，妻孥八人皆遇害。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Jurchens entered Zhending; Cui held them off with a lone army, and eight members of his wife and children were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Jurchens entered Zhending. Cui held them off with a lone army, and eight members of his family were killed.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，辟諸軍統製，宗澤命擊金人於南華，敗之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was recruited as commander of the armies; Zong Ze ordered him to strike the Jurchens at Nanhua, and he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyan he was recruited as commander of the armies. Zong Ze ordered him to attack the Jurchens at Nanhua, and he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 兼大名府路都總管兵馬鈐轄，擢知恩州。

translations.literal: He was concurrently given command of Daming Prefecture Route troops as Military Controller and was promoted to magistrate of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently placed in command of the Daming Prefecture Route forces as military controller and was promoted to prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 王善者，金之種落也。

translations.literal: Wang Shan was of Jurchen stock.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan was of Jurchen origin.

sentences.zh: 擁眾十萬，長驅兩河，遂襲恩。

translations.literal: Leading a force of one hundred thousand, he swept through the two He regions and then struck En.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of a force of one hundred thousand, he swept through the two He regions and then attacked Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 淬與長子仲剛拒戰，賊飛刃及淬，仲剛以身蔽刃，死之。

translations.literal: Cui and his eldest son Zhonggang resisted; the rebels hurled blades at Cui and Zhonggang shielded him with his body and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cui and his eldest son Zhonggang resisted. The rebels hurled blades at Cui, and Zhonggang shielded him with his own body and was killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，善復圍陳州，淬大敗善兵，拜宿州安撫使。

translations.literal: The next year Shan again besieged Chenzhou; Cui routed Shan's army and was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shan again besieged Chenzhou. Cui routed his army and was appointed pacification commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 李成叛，詔以淬為御營使、六軍都統、淮南招撫使討之，三戰三捷。

translations.literal: When Li Cheng rebelled, an edict appointed Cui Commissioner of the Imperial Camp, Commander-in-Chief of the Six Armies, and Pacification Commissioner for Huainan to suppress him; in three battles he won three victories.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cheng rebelled, an edict appointed Cui commissioner of the imperial camp, commander-in-chief of the six armies, and pacification commissioner for Huainan to suppress him. In three battles he won three victories.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金人犯采石，又檄淬回援建康。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens attacked Caishi, and Cui was again ordered by dispatch to return and relieve Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jurchens attacked Caishi, and Cui was again ordered by dispatch to return and relieve Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 淬將中軍，戚方將前，王燮將後。

translations.literal: Cui commanded the center, Qi Fang the vanguard, and Wang Xie the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Cui commanded the center, Qi Fang the vanguard, and Wang Xie the rear.

sentences.zh: 淬曰：「彼眾雖多，然止有二十艘，一艘不越五十人，每至不過千人。

translations.literal: Cui said: "Though their numbers are many, they have only twenty boats, each carrying no more than fifty men—each crossing brings no more than a thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Cui said, "Though their numbers are great, they have only twenty boats, each carrying no more than fifty men—each crossing brings no more than a thousand."

sentences.zh: 吾伏兵葭蘆翳薈間，俟其旋濟旋獲，前後不相知，訖濟，當盡獲矣。

translations.literal: "We shall hide troops among the reeds and dense thickets; as they cross and are captured one after another, front and rear unaware of each other, when the crossing is finished we shall capture them all."
translations.idiomatic: "We shall hide troops among the reeds and dense thickets. As they cross and are captured in turn, front and rear unaware of one another, once the crossing is complete we shall take them all."

sentences.zh: 」杜充不從，金兵遂犯板橋，諸軍皆潰，淬獨與戰，勢窮力盡，據胡床大罵，刃交於胸而色不動，與其從子仲敏俱死。

translations.literal: Du Chong would not agree; the Jurchen troops then attacked Banqiao; the armies all scattered; Cui alone continued fighting until his strength was exhausted; seated on a folding chair he cursed loudly; blades crossed his chest yet his expression did not change; he and his nephew Zhongmin both died.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong refused to agree. The Jurchen troops then attacked Banqiao, the armies scattered, and Cui alone kept fighting until his strength was spent. Seated on a folding chair, he cursed loudly. Blades crossed his chest, yet his expression never changed. He and his nephew Zhongmin both died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈拱衛大夫、明州觀察使，官其一子一婿。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Grand Master of the Palace Guard and Observation Commissioner of Mingzhou, and gave office to one son and one son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of Grand Master of the Palace Guard and observation commissioner of Mingzhou, and gave official posts to one son and one son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 黃友，字龍友，溫州平陽人。

translations.literal: Huang You, courtesy name Longyou, was a native of Pingyang in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang You, style name Longyou, was a native of Pingyang in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少不羈，十五入太學，語同輩曰：「大丈夫不能為國立功，亦造化中贅物耳。

translations.literal: From youth he was unrestrained; at fifteen he entered the Imperial Academy and told his fellows: "If a great man cannot establish merit for the state, he is but excess matter in the workings of creation."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was wild and unrestrained. At fifteen he entered the Imperial Academy and told his classmates, "If a great man cannot win merit for the state, he is nothing but excess matter in the workings of creation."

sentences.zh: 」因投筆西遊。

translations.literal: He thereupon cast aside his brush and traveled west.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon cast aside his brush and set out westward.

sentences.zh: 邊帥劉法一見奇之，延致門下。

translations.literal: The frontier commander Liu Fa, upon first meeting him, was struck by his talent and brought him into his household.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commander Liu Fa was struck by his talent at first meeting and brought him into his household.

sentences.zh: 會西鄙軍哄，都護高永年戰沒，友作七詩哀其忠。

translations.literal: When the western armies mutinied and Protector-General Gao Yongnian died in battle, You composed seven poems mourning his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the western armies mutinied and Protector-General Gao Yongnian died in battle, You composed seven poems mourning his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其後幕府奏功，沒永年之實，恤典不及。

translations.literal: Later the staff memorialized achievements but omitted Yongnian's actual deeds, and the condolence honors did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the staff memorialized achievements but omitted Yongnian's actual deeds, and the condolence honors due him were never granted.

sentences.zh: 其子以友詩進，徽宗覽之惻然，遂加贈諡。

translations.literal: His son presented You's poems; Emperor Huizong read them and was deeply moved, and additional posthumous honors and a title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yongnian's son presented You's poems. Emperor Huizong read them, was deeply moved, and granted additional posthumous honors and a title.

sentences.zh: 友亦免省試，登進士第，調永嘉、瑞安二縣主簿，攝華陰令，有政聲。

translations.literal: You was also exempted from the provincial examination, passed the jinshi, was assigned as recorder of Yongjia and Ruian counties, and acted as magistrate of Huayin with a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: You was also exempted from the provincial examination, passed the jinshi, served as recorder of Yongjia and Ruian counties, and acted as magistrate of Huayin, where he earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 方臘竊發，友同諸將收復，所至披靡。
